paras: The Aberdeen constable shooting was the pursuit of an unnamed Black man at Aberdeen on the morning of 24 August 1895, during which Constable Dawson fired several shots at him. The man, said to have shot a man at Lewisburg some time earlier, escaped, and the incident is known only from a single brief item in a Maysville, Kentucky, daily.

According to the Daily Public Ledger of Maysville, the man was wanted as the one who "shot a man at Lewisburg some time ago"; the item gives no name for him or for the man he was accused of shooting, and no date for that shooting.

On the morning of 24 August the man was seen at Aberdeen, and Constable Dawson and the town marshal of Aberdeen gave chase. Dawson fired several shots at him during the pursuit, but the man got away. The item does not say whether any of the shots struck him, and it names neither the county nor the state in which Aberdeen lay.
No report of a capture, arrest or any later proceeding was found in the coverage.

The Ledger ran the story as a single sentence among its local briefs, between a court fine and a notice about river obstructions. It referred to the man as "the darkey" and "Mr. Nigger" and stated the Lewisburg shooting as fact rather than as an accusation, while offering no comment on the constable's firing at a fleeing man.
No Black-press report of the incident was found.

reader.title: Aberdeen constable shooting (1895)
bases: Two officers, a constable and a town marshal, pursued a Black man and the constable fired several shots at him; no crowd is mentioned (A1).
Only one brief item reports the chase (A1); the other Maysville daily's local column of the same day does not mention it (A2), and no Black-press report was found.

accounts.label: Maysville local brief
accounts.gist: The man wanted for a Lewisburg shooting was seen at Aberdeen; the constable and town marshal chased him, the constable fired several shots, and he escaped.

framing.detail: No editorial comment on the shooting, but the item uses the slurs "darkey" and "Mr. Nigger" in a mocking tone and treats the accusation as fact ("The darkey who shot a man").

record_check.dossier: Not stated. The item names no county; the only "Butler" on the page is in a party ticket printed above it ("W. S. TAYLOR, of Butler"), which the record appears to have picked up by mistake.

Constable Dawson and the town marshal of Aberdeen; Dawson did the shooting.
